body:
## Summary

The coverage matrix has a tier for *"empty when it should not be"* and a verdict vocabulary for *"absent when it should not be"*, but **no way to record that a cell is correctly empty**. A wave whose survey deliberately elicited something the feature cannot compute is graded with the tier whose own docstring calls it a bug class:

```
dropped   source declared for the wave but the wave is missing /
          empty in the built table (the silent-drop bug class)
```
(`coverage_matrix.py:38-39`)

`VERDICTS = {"todo", "asked-not-distributed", "not-asked", "unsure"}` (`coverage_matrix.py:129`) and `load_verdicts` adjudicates **`absent`** cells only. Nothing adjudicates `dropped`.

## The concrete case that exposes it

GH #770: GhanaLSS's early waves elicited food **expenditure without quantity** (`u='Value'`, measured `Quantity == Expenditure` in 100.0% of 3,492,915 rows). Once the fabricated kg factor is removed, `food_prices` has no denominator for those rows and `_drop_unpriceable` removes them, so **six of seven `GhanaLSS,food_prices` cells go `sane → dropped`**.

That is the *correct* outcome — an honest empty beats a constant `2.035038` — but the matrix will then assert, permanently and with no way to annotate it, that a deliberate fix is an instance of "the silent-drop bug class". The next person to run `make matrix` sees six new red-ish cells and no reason.

This is not GhanaLSS-specific. Any wave that measures value but not quantity produces the same shape, and the corpus has more of them: 2005-06 alone is 966,373 such rows, and Panama carries 17,821.

## What is missing

A verdict vocabulary for `dropped` — the direct analogue of what `absent_verdicts.csv` already does — distinguishing:

| meaning | closes? |
|---|---|
| **correctly empty** — the instrument does not support this feature for this wave (value without quantity; a module that asks a different question) | yes |
| **empty pending machinery** — computable in principle, not yet implemented (e.g. #562 phase 3b's price→quantity imputation would repopulate these very cells) | no — stays visible |
| **genuinely dropped** — the silent-drop bug the tier was named for | no — a defect |

The third is what the tier means today; the first two are indistinguishable from it, and the first is arguably not a gap at all.

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

The repository's stated position is that a tier which cannot express a legitimate state gets discredited — the same argument that produced `undeclared` in #724/#725 (*"a denominator that omits the work you have not started is not a denominator"*) and the `not-asked` / `asked-not-distributed` split for `absent`. `dropped` is now in the position `absent` was in before verdicts existed: one label doing three jobs.

There is also an evidence-discipline point. `absent_verdicts.csv` **refuses a closing verdict without evidence** (`load_verdicts`), precisely because an unevidenced negative is unfalsifiable. Whatever is built for `dropped` should inherit that rule — "correctly empty" is exactly the kind of claim that would otherwise be asserted rather than shown.

## Suggested direction

Either extend `absent_verdicts.csv` to adjudicate `dropped` as well (one file, one loader, one evidence rule — the cell's tier disambiguates), or add a sibling file. The former looks cheaper and avoids a second convention.

Interim, if #770 lands before this: record the reasoning in `GhanaLSS/_/CONTENTS.org` so the six cells are at least explicable to a human, even though the matrix cannot express it.

Found while red-teaming #770. Refs #724, #725, #770, #562.

— Sue

comments.body: Six fresh instances of exactly this gap from today's corpus regrade (2026-09-09, `development` `d2729e81`): GhanaLSS `food_prices` 1987-88, 1988-89, 1991-92, 1998-99, 2005-06 and 2012-13 moved `sane` -> `dropped`. They are CORRECTLY empty: GLSS1-6 elicit food purchases by value only (currency-denominated `u` on 100 / 100 / 54 / 82 / 87 / 88 % of `food_acquired` rows by wave), and #770 (`71b6ce92`) stopped inferring a kg factor for those units, so the currency-per-currency "prices" that had graded `sane` are no longer fabricated -- `food_prices()` now serves 2016-17 (407,478 rows) alone. `dropped` is the wrong word for a cell that is empty because the instrument recorded no quantities; a verdict vocabulary for "correctly empty" (`not-asked` at the derived-table level, or a `dropped-by-design`) is what these six need. Until then they sit in the silent-drop queue looking like a defect.

**Ruling (@ligon, 2026-10-18)**, from the framework-backlog decision sheet: Yes. Add `correctly-empty` (closing, evidence required as for `not-asked`) and `empty-pending-machinery` (not closing) to the verdict vocabulary, keyed by tier. A fix agent may write the three GhanaLSS GLSS1-3 rows into `.coder/coverage/absent_verdicts.csv`, with evidence.

Scheduled for the overnight 2026-10-18 sweep.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
Fixed on `development` by PR #1132. Left open until the release merge to `master`; follow-ups are #1129-#1131.

**RULING (@ligon, 2026-10-19):** keep the GhanaLSS GLSS1/2 (1987-88, 1988-89) `food_prices` verdicts as `correctly-empty`, as merged in PR #1132.
- Neither survey records a household price, only amounts.
- An imputed price of Expenditure ÷ community price would re-serve `community_prices`.
- #562 3b as specified fills `food_quantities`, not `food_acquired`.

GLSS3 (1991-92) stays `empty-pending-machinery` (#1130).

title: No verdict vocabulary for `dropped`: a correctly-empty cell is graded as "the silent-drop bug class" with no way to say otherwise
